# Cross-Entry Integration Checklist: Issues — creation, detail and editing

**Purpose**: Validate that the requirements describing what this feature consumes from earlier entries, what it obliges them to deliver, and what four later entries will add to it, are complete, unambiguous and free of conflict — before the feature is decomposed into tasks
**Created**: 2026-08-31
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) · [plan.md](../plan.md) · [contracts/](../contracts/) · [docs/ROADMAP.md](../../../docs/ROADMAP.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

This is a **requirements-quality** review, not a verification pass. Every item asks whether something is *written well*, not whether code *works*.

## Requirement Completeness — what this feature consumes

- [ ] CHK001 Do the requirements distinguish the entries this feature **cannot be built without** from those it merely cites, rather than listing all of them in one dependency sentence? [Gap, Spec §Dependencies]
- [ ] CHK002 Is each consumed contract named at the granularity its provider's author would need — the predicate, the counter row's shape, the route, the header slot — rather than by entry number alone? [Completeness, Spec §Dependencies]
- [ ] CHK003 Are requirements stated for what this feature must do if a consumed contract arrives in a different shape than assumed — the counter's columns being the clearest case? [Gap, Spec §FR-013]
- [ ] CHK004 Is the module this feature extracts identified by something an R5 author could act on, given that R5 is unbuilt and its file layout is undecided? [Gap, Spec §FR-044]
- [ ] CHK005 Are the constraints this feature adds to a table another entry owns stated as requirements, or left to be discovered when the migration is written? [Gap, Spec §FR-005]

## Requirement Consistency — the dependency claims

- [ ] CHK006 Does the stated dependency set agree with the set the requirements actually exercise — is every entry listed as a dependency genuinely required, and is none required but unlisted? [Conflict, Spec §Dependencies]
- [ ] CHK007 Do the requirements agree with the roadmap's own dependency edge for this entry, and is any divergence recorded as a reconciliation rather than left implicit? [Consistency, Spec §Dependencies, Roadmap §R6]
- [ ] CHK008 Is the claim that this feature is the markdown subset's second call site consistent with every other statement about the subset's ownership, including the roadmap's? [Consistency, Spec §FR-044, §Reconciliations, Roadmap §1.1]
- [ ] CHK009 Are the requirements that reach into another entry's work consistent about who performs the reach — this feature, or the entry being reached into? [Consistency, Spec §FR-028, §FR-044]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK010 Is "every project-scoped screen that exists when this feature lands" resolvable to a definite set, or does it depend on a build order the requirements do not fix? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-028]
- [ ] CHK011 Is "the destination MUST be a route that exists when this feature lands" stated as a constraint on this feature or as an assumption about another? [Clarity, Spec §FR-060]
- [ ] CHK012 Is "adding no dependency" specific about which dependency ledger it refers to, and about whether an already-installed transitive package counts as added? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-044]
- [ ] CHK013 Is "promoted out of R5's feature directory" precise about the destination, or only about the origin? [Clarity, Spec §FR-044]

## Requirement Completeness — what later entries add

- [ ] CHK014 Is each of the four later entries' additions described precisely enough that its author could implement it without re-deriving the contract from this feature's code? [Completeness, Spec §Reconciliations, contracts/mutators.md]
- [ ] CHK015 Are requirements stated for how each cascade arm attaches, distinctly from what each arm removes? [Completeness, Spec §FR-059]
- [ ] CHK016 Is the obligation on later entries to extend the delete confirmation's stated size stated as a requirement on them, or only as a description of what will happen? [Clarity, Spec §FR-062]
- [ ] CHK017 Are requirements stated for whether this feature's own acceptance scenarios must continue to hold after each later entry reaches back into its mutators? [Gap]
- [ ] CHK018 Is the decision to build no extension points stated as a requirement with a rationale, so a later planner cannot read it as an oversight? [Completeness, Spec §Out of Scope]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK019 Is the criterion that another entry's scenarios pass unchanged after the extraction verifiable, given that those scenarios may themselves change before this feature lands? [Measurability, Assumption, Spec §SC-017]
- [ ] CHK020 Is there a measurable criterion for the mutator contracts later entries depend on, verifiable on this feature alone before any of them exists? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §SC-018]
- [ ] CHK021 Can "one implementation renders both" be objectively verified from the requirements, without inspecting the module layout? [Measurability, Spec §SC-017]

## Scenario Coverage & Boundaries

- [ ] CHK022 Are requirements defined for the case where this feature is built before an entry it depends on — or is that ordering excluded, and stated as excluded? [Gap, Spec §Dependencies]
- [ ] CHK023 Is every item deferred to a later entry attributed to exactly one entry, with no capability claimed by two or left unclaimed? [Consistency, Spec §Out of Scope]
- [ ] CHK024 Does the scope boundary agree with the roadmap's own R6 row in both directions — nothing in scope that the roadmap defers, nothing deferred that the roadmap assigns here? [Consistency, Spec §Out of Scope, Roadmap §R6]
- [ ] CHK025 Are the requirements this feature places on entries that are already specified but unbuilt recorded where those entries' authors will encounter them, rather than only here? [Traceability, Gap]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [ ] CHK026 Are the inherited constraints distinguished from the decisions this feature makes, clearly enough that a reviewer does not attribute an inherited rule to this entry? [Clarity, Spec §Inherited constraints]
- [ ] CHK027 Is each assumption about another entry's behaviour stated with the consequence of it being wrong, rather than as a bare assertion? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK028 Are the dependency-approval obligations this feature triggers — any package it must install, and any it must decline — stated in the requirements, or discovered only at planning? [Gap, Spec §FR-040, §FR-044]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- CHK006 and CHK001 are the pair worth reading first, and they point at the same sentence. The spec's *Dependencies* lists R3 among the entries this feature depends on transitively and names it as supplying "the accounts and the deactivation state the assignee pool filters on"; [plan.md](../plan.md) records that R3 is **not** a build precondition, because the flag this feature reads is a column on R1's table. Both readings are defensible — R3 is a product dependency and not a code one — which is exactly why the requirement should say which kind it means
- CHK001, CHK005 and CHK028 are answered in [plan.md](../plan.md) and [data-model.md](../data-model.md). That the answers exist is not the same as the requirement being specified
